start_here: Say to your AI: "Get the words spoken in the video vid-aaa from its captions and tell me what it teaches." It runs the captions command on your computer with yt-dlp and reads the transcript from the file it writes.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it asks yt-dlp for one video's captions and writes the words to one JSON file on your computer.
instructions: 1. Check that node and yt-dlp are installed (brew install yt-dlp) and clone the Workshop repository. No key is needed and nothing is sent to Trillion.
2. Give the video as an id or a link (tool:list-a-channels-latest-videos gives each video's item_id and url).

3. The AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:read-a-videos-captions"} and runs: node trillion-workshop/tools/research-a-creator-or-topic/do-work/research-from-this-computer.mjs captions --video vid-aaa --out captions.json. Add --langs en,en-orig to change the languages, --js-runtimes node when stderr_tail says yt-dlp needs a JavaScript runtime.

4. Read the last line, {"result": {video_id, url, parser, has_captions, char_count, stderr_tail, status, out}}, then the transcript in captions.json. Status ready means words; status empty means the video has none, and stderr_tail says why: tell the person that instead of guessing its words.

worked_examples.title: A video whose original-language captions are read first
worked_examples.ask: Get the words spoken in vid-aaa from its captions.
worked_examples.given: From tools/research-a-creator-or-topic/test/commands.test.mjs (the captions test, with yt-dlp stood in): yt-dlp leaves two caption files for vid-aaa, sub.en.json3 ("English words") and sub.en-orig.json3 ("Original words"). The AI runs: node trillion-workshop/tools/research-a-creator-or-topic/do-work/research-from-this-computer.mjs captions --video vid-aaa --out captions.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"video_id":"vid-aaa","url":"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vid-aaa","parser":"caption-json3","has_captions":true,"char_count":14,"stderr_tail":"","status":"ready","out":"captions.json"}} and captions.json holds "transcript":"Original words" (the original language is read before plain English). For a video with no captions, status is "empty", has_captions false, transcript "" and stderr_tail holds yt-dlp's reason.
